title: The Red Tide of 1892 and the Oysters Left on Ojima
conflicts: The slate's 1905 red tide (850,000 oysters, round pearls found among the dead) appears only on dealer/magazine pages and in Eunson's 1955 biography (not readable online), and is absent from Mikimoto's own 1907 and 1911 booklets, so the documented 1892 red tide was told instead. Start date (1888 per the tourism agency vs 1890 per the 1907 booklet), place of the red tide (Ago Bay vs Ise Bay), cause (AFP says a bacterial virus), who found the pearls (he, or he and Ume), and credit for round pearls (Mikimoto vs Mise and Nishikawa) all differ; the story follows the Japan Tourism Agency and attributes contested points.
notes: Episode changed from 1905 to 1892-93 (same founder, same kind of setback). The five-pearl count is from the tourism agency only and is attributed. The MLIT PDF/DOCX sources load but are not machine-readable by the checker; their text was extracted and read in full. Quote stance: affirms.
